title: Bond basics and the price of a bond
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b passed round 2 (0 blocking)
transcript_provenance: Publisher-uploaded English captions (NPTEL-NOC IITM YouTube channel, non-automatic track)

practice_sources.used_for: Review IV current-yield/YTM/pricing distinctions and the inverse price-yield relation; inspires original conceptual exercises.

source_uncertainties: Lecture 36 f0001 identifies Prof. Pramod Kumar Naik. No inference that all chapter recordings share one presenter is needed.
Lecture 36 f0027 gives the 100/800 current-income illustration without the remaining maturity needed for a finite-bond valuation; the chapter identifies that limitation.
Lecture 37 f0044/f0047 semiannual formula retains Fr instead of Fr/2 despite the annual coupon definition; the chapter derives and uses the required half-year coupon.

Lecture 38's displayed prices 946.1, 1194.5 and 848.5 differ from unrounded evaluations 945.737565, 1194.736753 and 847.538896. The first uses shown rounded factors; the other differences are preserved without guessing hidden factors.

Review IV f0042/f0045/f0046 states the correct inverse relation: a lower required yield raises present value and price, and a higher required yield lowers them. The chapter derives this relation for fixed positive payments.
The books named during the recordings were not consulted as open sources and are not cited as read.
No relied-on formula or example symbol remained unreadable in the full frames.

sections.section: Why an issuer borrows through bonds
sections.lecture_material: Debt financing and bondholder versus shareholder claims.
sections.research_extension: SEC debtor obligations and corporate creditor priority qualifications.
sections.teaching_construction: Distinguishes a contractual promise from the model assumption of payment.

sections.section: Read the contract before choosing a rate
sections.lecture_material: Face F, redemption M, annual coupon rate and remaining maturity.
sections.teaching_construction: Fund case, distinct observed price, timing assumptions, original cash-flow SVG.

sections.section: Bond classifications identify different payment promises
sections.lecture_material: Issuer, maturity, collateral, zero-coupon, callable and convertible classifications.
sections.research_extension: SEC collateral/conversion qualifications; FINRA call terms and sovereign credit risk.
sections.teaching_construction: Shows why the payment stream must reflect the selected contract.

sections.section: Separate payment risk, sale-price risk, and reinvestment risk
sections.lecture_material: Default, interest-rate, inflation, liquidity, reinvestment and call risk; broad versus issuer-specific influences.
sections.research_extension: SEC risk definitions and FINRA early-redemption consequences.
sections.teaching_construction: Maps each risk to a different failure of the fund's payment plan.

sections.section: Price the complete dated payment stream
sections.lecture_material: Annual fixed-payment present value and actuarial annuity notation.
sections.teaching_construction: Derives the annuity factor, zero-rate and one-year checks, five-year case and zero-coupon rate.

sections.section: Remaining maturity and rounding change the calculation
sections.lecture_material: Ten-year coupon pricing and a ten-year bond issued three years earlier; 13%, 10% and 18% inputs.
sections.teaching_construction: Reports displayed lecture prices separately from unrounded-model computations and checks directions.

sections.section: Why value falls with the required rate
sections.lecture_material: Inverse relation of required yield and price; premium/par/discount rules. Review IV repeats the inverse relation, which the chapter proves for a fixed payment schedule.
sections.teaching_construction: Strict derivative proof, identities relative to M and F, unequal-redemption counterexample, perpetuity limit.

sections.section: Current yield measures income relative to price
sections.lecture_material: Annual coupon divided by market price and the 1000/12%/800 example. L36 718-900 current-income illustration is additionally qualified.
sections.teaching_construction: Finite versus perpetual counterexample and fund's income ratio.

sections.section: Maturity yield is the rate implied by all promised payments
sections.lecture_material: Maturity yield as the discount rate balancing price with all promised payments.
sections.research_extension: FINRA mathematical YTM definition and gross-yield limitations.
sections.teaching_construction: Existence, uniqueness, sign, price/yield equivalence, yield ordering identity, fund yield.

sections.section: Solve a yield with a bracket and a price check
sections.lecture_material: Eight-year 9% coupon bond at price 800; trial rates and interpolation. Earlier L37 725-880 A/B comparison is additionally recomputed.
sections.teaching_construction: Bisection bracket invariant and error bound, residual limitation, exact A/B yields and qualified ranking.

sections.section: What the approximate-yield formula leaves out
sections.lecture_material: Weighted approximate yield formula and comparison with equal denominator weights.
sections.teaching_construction: Units, timing limitation, independent counterexample to universal accuracy, threshold-reversal exercise.

sections.lecture_material: Annual and semiannual pricing conventions and semiannual nominal-yield footnote.
sections.research_extension: FINRA annual coupon versus semiannual instalment convention.
sections.teaching_construction: Derives Fr/m and period-rate conversion; corrects missing half-coupon factor; original timing and numerical checks.

sections.section: A promised maturity yield does not fix terminal wealth
sections.lecture_material: Gross maturity yield, taxes/fees excluded, and early-sale return distinction; L36 1068-1083 reinvestment risk additionally developed.
sections.research_extension: FINRA gross yield versus holding outcome.
sections.teaching_construction: Terminal wealth identity, distinct reinvestment scenarios, changed sale horizon and payment failure.

sections.section: Resolve the fund's two decisions separately
sections.teaching_construction: Separates required-yield purchase criterion from terminal liability coverage, including the exact fee threshold.

sections.section: A reproducible price and yield calculation
sections.teaching_construction: Stdlib pricing and bisection implementation, explicit numeric and failure contracts, independent rational/direct-sum checks, exact stdout.
Six original reasoned exercises: derivation/counterexample, period conversion, income ratio, shortcut judgment, hypothetical default, liability design.

symbol_ledger.definition: Positive face/par reference amount for the coupon.
Positive redemption amount at scheduled maturity; not generally equal to F.
Annual coupon amount divided by F; local coupon-rate use differs from earlier inflation r.
Annual coupon amount Fr in the annual-payment model.
Positive integer remaining years; also annual coupon count until period conversion.
Positive observed/offered purchase price.
Constant effective annual valuation rate, greater than -1.
Discount factor (1+i)^(-1), evaluated at the rate specified in context.
Conditional value of the fixed dated payment schedule.
Sum of one-unit year-end payment values at the stated rate; n at rate zero.
A payment amount and its time measured in annual periods.
Current yield c/P_obs, annual income-to-price ratio; q remains available for geometric ratios.
Unique effective annual promised maturity yield solving P(i_y)=P_obs.
Local shorthand for P_obs=P(i_y) in the yield-ordering identity.
Lower rate, upper rate and number of bisection updates.
Heuristic approximation from annualized redemption gain and weighted capital.
Positive integer coupon instalments per year.
Number of remaining coupon periods, mn.
Effective rate per coupon period, greater than -1.
Coupon amount per period, Fr/m.
Nominal annual yield convertible m times, defined as mj.
Effective annual yield (1+j)^m-1.
Constant effective annual reinvestment rate for coupons; avoids earlier g growth-factor notation.
Wealth at maturity from redemption plus coupons accumulated under i_re.
